environmentMechanism_CLOSED.theMechanism: SAME font file, DIFFERENT text shaping. Both environments loaded the shipped faces - 43 registered, typeface shipped/shipped on both, same Chromium build 143.0.7499.4 from the same playwright-core pin, same axe 4.13.0, dpr 1 on both. The identical probe string measures 225.00px on Linux and 228.33px on Windows: 1.48% wider for the same face, which is glyph rasterisation and subpixel advance rounding rather than a different font. The consequence is visible in the geometry witness and it is exact: the FOOTER is byte-identical between the two runs (navFootTop 601, navFootHeight 299, provHeight 274, demonstratedTop 640 on both), and what moves is the NAV LIST - lastNavItemBottom 698 on Linux against 718 on Windows, 20px, and with it overlapPx 97 against 117 and navHiddenPx 98 against 118. A nav item's bottom edge sits 20px further down on Windows, across the footer figures' boxes, and axe compares the element stack at the centre of each text line box and refuses to composite a background when those stacks disagree. Partial overlap fires; full and none both resolve. 2 unresolved nodes on Linux, 134 on Windows.

theCorrectionToMyOwnCP1.whatCP1Said: the divergence is font metrics, and specifically WHETHER THE REMOTE WEBFONT RESOLVED.
theCorrectionToMyOwnCP1.whatTheAuthoritativeMeasurementSays: the class was right and the specific cause was wrong. Both environments resolve the webfont. CP1's arm - webfont blocked (0 nodes) against webfont allowed (88 nodes) on one machine - proved that font metrics drive the finding, which is true and is what made the geometry witness worth shipping. It did NOT prove that CI was in the blocked state, and I had no way to know from that machine. The real difference is shaping of the same face.
theCorrectionToMyOwnCP1.whyThisIsRecordedRatherThanEdited: DEV_PROCESS 3.2a: a correction carries the same evidentiary standard as the claim it corrects. This one is quoted from the two runs' own output above. CP1 is left as written, because a checkpoint that gets edited after the fact stops being a record of what was known when.

howTheContractNowCarriesTheVariance: the typeface witness and the geometry witness print on EVERY run, at the top and at the bottom, so two disagreeing machines are diagnosed from one log line rather than reproduced. That is what closed this mechanism.

Linux CI is DECLARED the figure of record in src/a11y-gate.mjs and in the workflow file; every other run prints 'INDICATIVE RUN, NOT THE FIGURE OF RECORD', pass or fail, and names which half of its findings do not transfer (colour transfers exactly, geometry does not).

the knife-edge class is adjudicated BY SUBJECT rather than by a count three environments put at 0, 2 and 134. A node on a new element fails; the same elements at a different count do not; the count is printed either way.
a run whose typeface did not land, or landed on only some scans, is REFUSED - a scan of a rendering this product does not ship is not a measurement of this product.

theCoordinatorsScopeADDITION_takenMidFli.whatIVERIFIEDRatherThanAccepted: all of it, at source, because DEV_PROCESS 3.2 says the brief's numbers are the planner's and reporting one as wrong is a successful outcome, and 3.2a says a correction carries the same evidentiary standard as the claim it corrects.

CONFIRMED.theRatio: 1.856:1 light and 1.737:1 dark, computed independently - compositing the resolved background by walking ancestors and applying the sRGB relative-luminance formula, not asking axe. K1 reported 1.855 and 1.737. Two independent computations agreeing to the third decimal. The pair is light rgb(174, 186, 197) on rgb(246, 248, 250) and dark rgb(59, 72, 84) on rgb(24, 33, 42), at 400 13px, so the requirement is 4.5:1. This is a real defect and it is roughly 40% of the floor.
CONFIRMED.theViewportPointAboutPOK: at 1440x900, 0 of 7 rendered .p-ok elements are in the viewport, so axe evaluates none of them. K1's direction is exactly right.

CORRECTED_1_theBucket.claim: the defect is hiding in axe's INCOMPLETE bucket, and the gate adjudicates it at a ceiling of 1 while the real figure is 44.
CORRECTED_1_theBucket.measured: it is in NO bucket. Cross-referenced on ELEMENT IDENTITY via axe.run({elementRef: true}) rather than on selector strings: of the 84 rendered .sep elements per theme, axe reports 84 as NOT EVALUATED and 0 as violation, pass or incomplete, in both themes.
CORRECTED_1_theBucket.andTheFortyFourIsADifferentFinding: the 44-per-theme incomplete nodes are on #nav-demonstrated and #nav-sources-rule - navFig axe={"incomplete":44,"pass":2} - which is the population the ledger's entry actually names. The two findings had been merged. .sep is a child of .prov; the nav figures ARE .prov elements; they are not the same subject.
CORRECTED_1_theBucket.whyItIsInNoBucket: established by bisect on ONE element in one page in one run with the character as the only variable: text "|" -> NOT EVALUATED; "X" -> incomplete; "||" -> NOT EVALUATED; "XY" -> VIOLATION. axe-core excludes punctuation-only text from color-contrast by design, at axe.js:28714-28726, `var removeUnicodeOptions = { emoji: true, nonBmp: false, punctuations: true }` feeding hasRealTextChildren, which returns false once the visible text is empty after punctuation is stripped - so colorContrastMatches never accepts the element as a candidate. That is axe working as documented, and it is a far worse problem than a ceiling set too low: no ceiling, no adjudication and no environment would ever have caught it.

CORRECTED_2_theAdjudicationIsNotRefuted.claim: the adjudication's stated reasoning - that it reads against a solid ground - is refuted by direct computation for these children.
CORRECTED_2_theAdjudicationIsNotRefuted.measured: not for its own subjects. #nav-demonstrated and #nav-sources-rule compute to 5.559:1 and 6.887:1 in light and 5.232:1 and 7.494:1 in dark, every one comfortably over 4.5:1. G-95's adjudication is CORRECT for the elements it names: axe cannot composite through the sticky overlap, and the composited pair is fine. The 1.737 belongs to .sep, which the adjudication never covered and which axe never evaluates.
CORRECTED_2_theAdjudicationIsNotRefuted.whyThisMattersMoreThanBeingRight: the report was wrong in the safe direction and the finding underneath it was real and larger. Both are only visible if the number is RECOMPUTED rather than read, which is exactly the control the coordinator asked for and which now exists.

CORRECTED_3_theCounts.claim: 874 .sep elements per theme across all 23 surfaces; 7 of 308 p-ok elements in viewport at 900.
CORRECTED_3_theCounts.measuredWithFourStatedDenominators: for .sep, per theme, summed over the 23 surfaces: 460 present in the DOM, 84 RENDERED (the remainder sit in lenses that are display:none), 83 in viewport at 1440x900, 84 at full extent. For .p-ok, per theme: 154 in the DOM, 7 rendered, 0 in viewport at 1440x900.
CORRECTED_3_theCounts.reconciliation: 154 x 2 themes = 308, which is K1's p-ok denominator, so that figure is the DOM population across both themes and my 7 is the rendered population in one. K1's in-viewport 7 does not reproduce at 900 in my run, where it is 0; 7 is what I measure at full extent. For .sep I cannot reconstruct 874 from any denominator I measured - 460 x 2 themes is 920 - so it is reported as UNRECONCILED rather than guessed at. DEV_PROCESS 1.4: two numbers that should agree and do not is a free finding, and rounding it off is the one thing not allowed.
CORRECTED_3_theCounts.whyNoneOfThisChangesTheConclusion: every denominator agrees the defect is on every surface in the product, and the RATIO - the thing that decides whether it is a WCAG failure - reproduced exactly.

whatIBUILTInResponse.1_aSecondInstrument: the scanner now composites backgrounds and computes WCAG ratios itself, for declared element groups, independent of axe and therefore of axe's exclusion set. It is deliberately conservative: it computes only where the answer is unambiguous - opaque foreground, opaque background reached without crossing an image, a gradient, a filter or a translucent layer, and an element whose own centre hit-tests back to itself - and everything else is counted as COULD NOT COMPUTE and reported, never scored clean and never scored as a failure. It applies the large-text threshold rather than one number. It excludes [aria-hidden=true] text and COUNTS what it excludes, because an exclusion nobody can see the size of is indistinguishable from a blind spot - which is the entire lesson of this finding.
whatIBUILTInResponse.2_adjudicationsCarryAMeasuredBasisAndAre: a REVIEW_ITEMS entry that claims a pair reads acceptably now carries measuredRatio and a threshold, the scanner recomputes exactly those subjects on every run, and the verdict REFUSES the entry when the run's own measurement falls below the threshold and prints a STALE note when it drifts from the recorded figure while still clearing. An adjudication is a claim about a number; the number is now checked rather than believed.
whatIBUILTInResponse.3_bothClassesCarryPlants: punctuation-contrast plants a low-contrast punctuation-only glyph, which is the class axe cannot see; adjudication-refuted repaints the adjudicated subjects below their threshold and leaves the ledger untouched, so the gate must refuse its own entry. Both fire at the verdict level on the bare-Node job as well.

theARIAHIDDENQUESTION_myAnswerAndTheEvid.recommendation: AGREE, with one measured caveat and one condition. aria-hidden="true" on the .sep span alone is the right fix: the glyph is a visual separator carrying no information a screen reader needs, the surrounding text stays parseable without it, and text that is pure decoration is outside 1.4.3's scope. It is a web/ edit and this lane has not made it.
theARIAHIDDENQUESTION_myAnswerAndTheEvid.theCaveatThatMattersAndIsMEASURED: aria-hidden does NOT satisfy axe. Bisected in the same run: an element with real text at a failing pair returns VIOLATION with aria-hidden=true set exactly as it does without it. So aria-hidden is a correctness fix and an accessibility-tree fix, not a tool-silencing fix - and the only reason it will read as resolved here is that THIS gate's own exclusion set is declared and counts what it excludes.
theARIAHIDDENQUESTION_myAnswerAndTheEvid.theCondition: if the product wants the separator to stay in the accessibility tree, then the decoration exception does not apply and the colour must go to 4.5:1 instead. One or the other, not neither.
theARIAHIDDENQUESTION_myAnswerAndTheEvid.routedNotTaken: web/index.html and web/shell.css are named untouchable in this dispatch and two sibling lanes are live in web/. The finding is carried in the ledger with its measurement, its owner and its removal condition, so it cannot be lost.

twoFailOpensFoundINMYOWNFIX_byRunningItR: the unresolved bucket was aggregated per RULE while adjudications are per rule AND REASON, so the shortTextContent entry pinned at 1 was compared against the whole rule's 44, and the elmPartiallyObscuring SUBJECT set was tested against targets belonging to the other reason. Both wrong in the same run. Fixed by splitting counts and targets by reason at the point axe reports them.

the set of elements 'axe already looked at' was collected from EVERY rule in the run, so a span that merely passed aria-allowed-attr counted as having had its contrast judged. The effect was total: the sweep computed 4,908 elements, found 341 below threshold, and reported ZERO of them. A silent fail-open inside the instrument built to catch silent fail-opens. Fixed by scoping to color-contrast and color-contrast-enhanced.

NEITHER was visible from reading the code and both were obvious the first time the gate was run end to end. Recorded because it is the same lesson the row exists for: a control is what it does, not what it says.

whatREMAINS.1_theLedgerMustBePinnedFromTHEAUTHORITAT: the first CI run failed on this branch, correctly and usefully: both waivers pinned from Windows numbers, and Linux CI - the environment this lane just declared the figure of record - reports color-contrast at 0 nodes on every arm, so the ratchet's zero arm fired with 'the waiver's cause is gone'. That is the gate refusing to let a number from a non-authoritative machine set a ceiling, which is the control working on its author. The ledger is being re-pinned from the CI run of the fixed head.
whatREMAINS.2_anOpenRECONCILIATION_notRoundedOff: Windows reports 5 color-contrast nodes on light@full-extent (the .p-ok 4.444:1 pair) and Linux reports 0, with coverage 100% at full extent on both. A hex pair is not a function of the operating system, so the colours cannot differ. The candidate I could not eliminate inside this lane: axe's matcher requires a text rect to overlap the box of EVERY overflow-hidden ancestor, and div.panel is one of those with a height of 295px - a 20px layout shift can push a table row outside the PANEL's clip while it is still inside the viewport, so my coverage figure, which is measured against the VIEWPORT box, would read 100% while axe still declines the element. If that is right then 'full extent covers 6198/6198' is true of the viewport and NOT of every clipping box, and the coverage figure needs the inner-clip axis added. Named here rather than smoothed over; the second instrument measures those elements regardless of axe, which is what keeps the defect visible while this is settled.
